meta.purpose: A decision queue, not a to-do list. Each proposal says what it would change, what it costs, what it risks, and — the part that matters — which earlier question has to be answered first. A reviewer can approve a row without reading the whole site.
meta.how_to_use: Read the 'depends on' column. Anything depending on Q-03 or Q-14 cannot be approved first, because approving it would spend effort on traffic that earns nothing.
meta.recommended_first: S-01 and S-02, because they are free, reversible, and unblock the rest.

suggestions.title: Confirm all five links are tagged for shopnow047c-20, then test one click and read the report
suggestions.why: All five destinations are now known (3 Air Fryers + 2 Meat Thermometers). What is still unknown is whether clicks on them are attributed to shopnow047c-20. Until one real click shows up in the Associates report, the site is sending readers somewhere that may not pay.
suggestions.effort: about 20 minutes of dashboard work plus one click
suggestions.risk: Low. Links can be swapped without changing any prose.

suggestions.title: Replace short links with validated tagged Special Links, and keep both values
suggestions.why: The short-link indirection caused intermittent /checkpoint/continue gating on P-01 and P-04 (FLG-004) and makes attribution hard to audit. Pointing at the validated Amazon listing with the Associates tag makes every link checkable while keeping the submitted link in the register as the historical record.
suggestions.risk: Low. Reversible. Never merge intended_asin with observed_asin.

suggestions.title: Name a real editor, or keep the current modest checklist voice
suggestions.why: Right now the site says nothing about who wrote it, which a careful reader notices immediately. A named person with an accurate bio is the cheapest credibility available.
suggestions.risk: None, provided the bio describes work that actually happened. Claiming hands-on testing that did not occur would convert this site from careful to deceptive.

suggestions.title: Add one genuinely tested product comparison — bought, used, and photographed
suggestions.why: This is the single biggest available jump in both usefulness and organic search potential. Real heating measurements, probe response timings in ice water and boiling water, a real cleanup test and real photographs would separate this publication from every synthetic review site.
suggestions.risk: Cost. Also, FTC and Amazon rules require the review to be genuine, so the testing must actually happen before the page exists.
suggestions.recommendation: The highest-value single investment on this list

suggestions.title: Connect the Product Advertising API / Creators API before showing any price or rating
suggestions.why: It is the only compliant route to live price, availability and rating, and those are the three things shoppers look for before clicking.
suggestions.effort: an application, plus qualifying sales to unlock API access on most accounts
suggestions.risk: None to the site. The blocker is that eligibility requires sales, which requires traffic, which is what the guides and Search Console build.
suggestions.recommendation: Start the application once S-01 confirms attribution

suggestions.title: Switch on measurement before writing more guides
suggestions.why: Seven guides now cover the core buyer questions across both categories (air fryers and meat thermometers). The next guide should be picked from measured Search Console queries and click data rather than instinct.
suggestions.effort: an hour of setup, then 2–4 weeks of waiting for data
suggestions.risk: Low. The client is already written and stays silent until switched on.

suggestions.title: Verify the property in Search Console and submit sitemap.xml
suggestions.why: Without this, search engines have no owner-verified signal and the topic question can never be answered with real query data.
suggestions.risk: None. Requires the owner's Google account, so it cannot be done by an agent.

suggestions.title: Decide whether to keep the two-category focus (3 Air Fryers + 2 Meat Thermometers)
suggestions.why: Now that P-04 resolved to the ThermoMaven instant-read thermometer, the catalogue splits naturally into 3 Air Fryers and 2 Meat Thermometers (instant-read vs. wireless multi-probe). That pairing makes strong editorial sense — a thermometer answers the doneness question an air fryer cannot — or you can narrow exclusively to air fryers.
suggestions.risk: Low either way. Both categories now have dedicated pages and tailored guides.
suggestions.recommendation: Keep both categories — the pairing is genuinely useful and already structured cleanly

suggestions.title: Add a reader-facing 'ask a question' capture, once a privacy notice exists
suggestions.why: The most useful input for the next guide is a real question from a real reader. It also feeds the editorial pipeline with something better than keyword guesses.
suggestions.effort: an hour plus a form endpoint
suggestions.risk: Handling personal data creates obligations that do not currently exist on this site. Do not ship a form before the privacy notice does.
suggestions.recommendation: After the privacy notice, not before

suggestions.title: Run a monthly dated link & listing re-verification
suggestions.why: Amazon listings change, short links can be gated or retired (FLG-004), and affiliate pages age badly when left unchecked. A visible monthly desk log is cheap and proves human maintenance.
suggestions.risk: None. The build already supports dated desk notes.

suggestions.title: Do not add more synthetic guides until S-04 or S-06 lands
suggestions.why: This is a recommendation to stop, which belongs on a suggestions page. Seven grounded guides already cover format, capacity, cleanup, multi-function trade-offs, thermometer types, meal prep and holiday hosting. More unmeasured prose dilutes focus without adding evidence.
suggestions.risk: Opportunity cost if a specific seasonal gap appears before query data arrives.
suggestions.recommendation: The least popular and most important item on this page

suggestions.title: Replace illustrative imagery with real photographs of the actual products
suggestions.why: The site currently labels every photograph as an illustration. That is honest, but it is also a visible ceiling on how convincing the pages can be. Real photographs of the real units, taken by the owner, remove the caveat entirely.
suggestions.effort: an afternoon with a phone and a window
suggestions.risk: Low. Requires the products to be in hand.

suggestions.title: Retire or archive legacy parallel-edition files in the repo root
suggestions.why: Earlier parallel sessions left legacy files (dashboard.html, products.html, guides.html, crisp/) alongside the canonical Crisp & Counter build. They are currently excluded from sitemap.xml and navigation, but archiving or removing them eliminates duplicate URLs if a crawler discovers them.
suggestions.risk: Low once confirmed nobody bookmarks the legacy filenames.
suggestions.recommendation: Approve after verifying no external links point to the legacy filenames

suggestions.title: Deploy the self-hosted analytics collector (server/collect.js) on a first-party host
suggestions.why: GitHub Pages is static, so server/collect.js cannot run there directly. Deploying it on a lightweight first-party host behind a published privacy notice turns on the five defined events without third-party trackers or cookies.
suggestions.risk: Low, provided the privacy notice and retention policy are published first.
suggestions.recommendation: Do together with S-06 and S-07
